bifrost: none for apps. The installer partitions real disks (springboard/src/installer/plan.rs, springboard/src/installer/disks.rs). tools/arch-vm.sh uses truncate, mkfs.ext4 and mount -o loop, but only for the developer VM harness, not the desktop.
summary: DiskImageKit creates, opens and stacks disk images (ASIF, RAW, layered) for Virtualization. BifrOSt has no app-facing API for disk images, and the Files app has no ISO or image mount path. The only loop-mount code is build and test tooling.

features.note: Wave 3 (w3-diskimagekit, parity/integration cf8e852d): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No SDK type creates an image file of a given size and block size.
ASIF is Apple's sparse image format. Linux has no equivalent; RAW or qcow2 would need a new format path.

Wave 3 (w3-diskimagekit, parity/integration cf8e852d): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. Opening an image as a block device needs a loop device or a userspace mount through the system layer, and apps get no API for it.
Layered stacking is part of Apple's image format. Linux has no direct counterpart, so an overlay design would be new work.

Wave 3 (w3-diskimagekit, parity/integration cf8e852d): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No types for image format or block size exist in the SDK.

features.note: Wave 3 (theme-29, parity/integration cf8e852d): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No app-facing resize call. The filesystem inside the image is not resized.

features.note: Wave 3 (theme-29, parity/integration cf8e852d): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. No app-facing VM storage API. The test VMs are developer tooling only.

Wave 5 (theme-21, parity/integration 93f283b0): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. Depends on the create, open and stack APIs above.

gaps: No SDK API to create, open or mount disk image files (RAW or ISO) for apps. Apps cannot do what DiskImageKit does for a user opening an ISO or disk image in Files.
Files has no ISO or image mount action, and no removable or mounted-volume eject path (springboard/apps/files/src).
No loop-device or userspace mount service in the system layer exposed to apps. The loop mount in tools/arch-vm.sh is developer tooling only.
No image metadata, resize or block-size API.
ASIF and stacked-layer formats are Apple-only. Their status is n/a, and a Linux format would need its own design.
